sentences.text: Toru Nakashima, born in 1963 in Aichi Prefecture, graduated from the engineering faculty of the University of Tokyo in 1986 and joined Sumitomo Bank, the predecessor of Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, that same year.

He held posts including head of the Shin-Yokohama corporate banking department, head of retail banking and head of corporate planning, becoming an executive officer at SMBC in 2014, a senior managing executive officer in 2016, a director and senior managing executive officer of the holding company in 2019, and deputy president in April 2023.

sentences.quote: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc. named Toru Nakashima as chief executive officer, turning to an experienced insider to lead Japan's second-largest bank following the death of his predecessor.
sentences.text: He was named chief executive officer of Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group effective December 1, 2023, after the death of his predecessor Jun Ohta.
He currently serves as director and president, representative executive officer, and Group CEO, and has also been a director of Jefferies Financial Group since August 2024.

sentences.text: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMBC Group) lifted profit attributable to owners of parent 34.4 percent to about 1.58 trillion yen, with return on net assets improving to 10.4 percent, a record alongside EPS of 412 yen that met its previous medium-term targets.

sentences.quote: SMFG estimates each hike of 25 basis points boosts its annual earnings by 100 billion yen
sentences.text: Japanese rate normalisation is a direct earnings lever, as SMFG estimates each 25 basis point policy rate hike boosts annual earnings by 100 billion yen.

A new three-year plan from FY2026 targets improved capital efficiency through business portfolio transformation and a medium- to long-term ROTE of around 15 percent, comparable to major U.S. and European institutions, with net income in the mid-2 trillion yen range.
Growth is skewed to efficient, low capital-intensive businesses such as asset management and transaction banking.
Capital returns are rising: annual dividends of 157 yen per share, a 38 percent payout ratio, and a buyback of up to 180 billion yen with shares cancelled.
